touches.text: Owns the inspectors and gates (9.4): everything in the code pipeline that checks. The exception is diagnostic_inspector, which is base's (17.1).
Runs a proof as its own process and writes a validation record (claim, caller, date, method, verdict, evidence, falsifier, horizon).

Seals: one current validation per proof, beside the proof. A seal holds while the code it measured is unchanged. [Q#90: A proof's seal is one record, so the newest OS to seal replaces the other's, and a proof with teeth for both OSes reds on every single OS. Measured 2026-11-12: a Windows reseal of a mixed proof overwrote the Linux seal. Do seals go per OS (validations/<os>/, or an OS key in the record), or is one OS the sealing box?]

The ticket IS its own manager. It carries its workflow and status, and asks each gate whether it can transit. If refused, it gets itself back to design for fixing. If no handler is available to ask, it throws a trouble and waits until we decide. Design is CC and Akien. Akien, 2026-11-11, Q#85: "you and me. later there will be a specific agent for it, but that's so far off we're not even thinking about it now except 'after the outline is implemented'." So until then a refused ticket waits in the trouble lane, which both of us read when a session opens, and nothing posts to a design verb that no machine answers.

Commit often. WHY: so we never wind up with stray files or incomplete work. [Q#94: A crossing into PROVEME refuses while anything in either tree is uncommitted (working_tree_clean, widened by ticket c1cca2e3dc23 on your 8w, F11 and 8x; unclaimed dirt refuses too, 8u). So with peers on one box, one peer's ticket records (another ticket's log/state, the artifact journal) block every other peer's crossing. Measured 2026-11-12: 3195b3b834bc's PROVEME was refused twice on the Dell, over d692ef650534's records and then the orchestrator's. Do records that artifact.locate claims for ANOTHER ticket stop blocking (unclaimed dirt and any code dirt still refuse), or does the whole-tree rule stand and peers serialise their crossings per box?]

artifact: the one door a record of truth changes through, and the journal of who came through it (hash-chained, caller read from the kernel). WHY: errors are permanent in records of truth (Law 7), and the journal is what shows a record moved by hand. USERS: everyone who writes a record. [Q#91: The caller class is read from the kernel's cgroup path, so on Windows it reads null and the class comes only from env vars (CAIRN_USER, CLAUDECODE, CAIRN_OPERATOR); gate cannot be reached, and 3 teeth in test_artifact_door.py say UNRAN. Measured 2026-11-12: the Windows parent process chain does show claude.exe above a shell. Is Windows a first-class caller platform (an exe-name chain: claude.exe is cc, a console with no claude above it is akien, a service session is gate), or env-fallback only?]
validation_store: reads and writes seals. USERS: the tester.
